# Code map: where things are

<!-- Written by tools/gen-code-map.mjs (npm run map). Do not edit this file: edit tools/code-map/ and the comments in the code, then run the command. -->

This page answers one question: **I see something in the app; which file is responsible for it?** It is for the owner, for anyone who reads or changes the code, and for AI agents that work in it. It is written by a script from the code and from a hand-kept list, so it stays true: `npm run map` writes it again, and the unit tests fail when it is out of date.

## How to find the code for something you see

Try these in order. Most searches end at step 1 or 2.

1. **Look it up by name.** The section [Where is … ?](#where-is--) lists what a person sees or does, in plain words, with the files behind it. It starts with its headings (Sidebar and shell, Settings, Player menus, Subtitles …): go to the heading first, then search (Ctrl+F) for the word you would use for the thing. A common word such as "subtitle" or "language" appears in many rows; the heading tells you which one is yours, and each row's note says what is next to it.
2. **Start from the address.** The address bar says which screen you are on. [The screens](#the-screens) gives the page file for every address. A page file is short: it names the parts the screen is made of, and each part is a file in the same folder.
3. **Start from the element itself.** Right-click the thing in the browser and choose **Inspect**. In the panel that opens, look at the highlighted element and the ones around it for an attribute that starts with `data-`, such as `data-pref-id="UserInterfaceLanguage"` or `data-player-button="settings"`. [Markers in the page](#markers-in-the-page) says which files write each one. Searching the code for the value (`UserInterfaceLanguage`) finds the exact place.
4. **Start from the words on the screen.** Every visible text has a key. Many rows of "Where is … ?" already name it. Otherwise search `src/i18n/locales/en.json` (texts the TV app also has) and `src/i18n/extra/en.json` (texts only the web has, keys starting with `web_`) for the English words, then search `src/` for the key. To change the words themselves, change them in that file.
5. **Read the folder.** [Every file of the source folder](#every-file-of-the-source-folder) lists each file with a sentence about what it does.

## Three things that save a wrong turn

- **A thing is often made of two files: where it is used and what it is built from.** A screen's own folder (under `src/features`) decides *what* is shown; the shared parts in `src/ui` decide *how* a dialog, a card, a row or a button looks and behaves everywhere. Example: the language list in Settings is opened by `src/features/settings/LanguagePreference.tsx`, and the box it sits in is the shared `src/ui/overlays/DialogPopup.tsx`. A change to how one dialog looks belongs in the first; a change to how all dialogs look belongs in the second.
- **The look is in the stylesheet beside the component.** `Name.tsx` says what is there; `Name.module.css` says its colour, size, spacing, transparency and motion. Colours are never written in a component: they come from the theme (`src/theme`).
- **An effect has no element of its own.** Something that slides, fades, grows, darkens or flashes is not a thing you can right-click. Find the element it happens to, then look in that element's stylesheet for `transition`, `animation`, `transform`, `opacity` or a `gradient`. When a thing appears and disappears, the line that decides it is in the component that places it (its parent), not in the thing itself.
- **Much of what you see is copied from the TV app on purpose.** When something looks odd, the comment at the top of its file usually says whether it follows the TV app (and where: `W/...` is a path in the TV app's source) or is a web addition. [DEVIATIONS.md](DEVIATIONS.md) lists every difference.

## Keeping this page true

- The lists of files, screens and markers are read from the code on every run. The sentence beside a file is the first sentence of the comment at its top (or on the first thing it exports): to improve a line here, improve that comment.
- The section "Where is … ?" comes from `tools/code-map/where.json` and the folder lines from `tools/code-map/folders.json`. Add a row when you add something a person can see, and when you had to search for something: the next person should not have to.
- `npm run map` writes the page; `npm run test` checks that it is current and that every file it names exists.

## The screens

Every address of the app and the file of its page (from the table at the top of [`src/app/routes.tsx`](../src/app/routes.tsx), the only place where routes are declared).

| Address | Page | Layout | Screen of the TV app |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/setup/servers [?next]` | [`features/setup/ServerListPage.tsx`](../src/features/setup/ServerListPage.tsx) | setup | SetupDestination.ServerList |
| `/setup/users [?next]` | [`features/setup/UserListPage.tsx`](../src/features/setup/UserListPage.tsx) | setup | SetupDestination.UserList(server) |
| `/setup/login [?username&mode&next]` | [`features/setup/LoginPage.tsx`](../src/features/setup/LoginPage.tsx) | setup | login dialog (SwitchUserContent) |
| `/` | [`features/home/HomePage.tsx`](../src/features/home/HomePage.tsx) | shell | Home |
| `/home/row/:rowId [?position]` | [`features/home/MoreHomeRowPage.tsx`](../src/features/home/MoreHomeRowPage.tsx) | shell | MoreHomeRow |
| `/search [?q]` | [`features/search/SearchPage.tsx`](../src/features/search/SearchPage.tsx) | shell | Search(query) |
| `/favorites` | [`features/browse/FavoritesPage.tsx`](../src/features/browse/FavoritesPage.tsx) | shell | Favorites |
| `/item/:itemId [?song]` | [`features/detail/MediaItemPage.tsx`](../src/features/detail/MediaItemPage.tsx) | shell | MediaItem (page dispatches on type) |
| `/series/:itemId [?season&episode]` | [`features/detail/SeriesOverviewPage.tsx`](../src/features/detail/SeriesOverviewPage.tsx) | shell | SeriesOverview (season/episode = ids) |
| `/library/:itemId [?tab]` | [`features/browse/CollectionFolderPage.tsx`](../src/features/browse/CollectionFolderPage.tsx) | shell | MediaItem(CollectionFolder/UserView/Folder) |
| `/library/:itemId/filtered [?type&filter&collectionType&recursive]` | [`features/browse/FilteredCollectionPage.tsx`](../src/features/browse/FilteredCollectionPage.tsx) | shell | FilteredCollection |
| `/grid  (location state ItemGridState)` | [`features/browse/ItemGridPage.tsx`](../src/features/browse/ItemGridPage.tsx) | shell | ItemGrid |
| `/recordings/:itemId` | [`features/livetv/RecordingsPage.tsx`](../src/features/livetv/RecordingsPage.tsx) | shell | Recordings |
| `/livetv` | [`features/livetv/LiveTvPage.tsx`](../src/features/livetv/LiveTvPage.tsx) | shell | (Live TV collection, drawer entry) |
| `/discover` | [`features/discover/DiscoverPage.tsx`](../src/features/discover/DiscoverPage.tsx) | shell | Discover |
| `/discover/more/:type` | [`features/discover/DiscoverMorePage.tsx`](../src/features/discover/DiscoverMorePage.tsx) | shell | DiscoverMoreResult |
| `/discover/:mediaType/:tmdbId` | [`features/discover/DiscoveredItemPage.tsx`](../src/features/discover/DiscoveredItemPage.tsx) | shell | DiscoveredItem |
| `/home/settings` | [`features/home/HomeSettingsPage.tsx`](../src/features/home/HomeSettingsPage.tsx) | fullscreen | HomeSettings |
| `/settings` | [`features/settings/SettingsPage.tsx`](../src/features/settings/SettingsPage.tsx) | fullscreen | Settings(BASIC) |
| `/settings/subtitles [?hdr]` | [`features/settings/SubtitleSettingsPage.tsx`](../src/features/settings/SubtitleSettingsPage.tsx) | fullscreen | SubtitleSettings(hdr) |
| `/settings/topic/:topic` | [`features/settings/SettingsTopicPage.tsx`](../src/features/settings/SettingsTopicPage.tsx) | fullscreen | (web: one subject of Settings; upstream's Advanced, Experimental and UserAppPreferences rows live here) |
| `/settings/:screen` | [`features/settings/SettingsPage.tsx`](../src/features/settings/SettingsPage.tsx) | fullscreen | Settings(screen) (screensaver, skip_segments, hdr_formats; advanced, experimental and user redirect to their subjects) |
| `/play/:itemId [?t&transcode&shuffle]` | [`features/playback/PlaybackPage.tsx`](../src/features/playback/PlaybackPage.tsx) | fullscreen | Playback (t = start ms) |
| `/play/list/:itemId [?index&shuffle&recursive&sort&order&filter]` | [`features/playback/PlaybackListPage.tsx`](../src/features/playback/PlaybackListPage.tsx) | fullscreen | PlaybackList |
| `/now-playing` | [`features/music/NowPlayingPage.tsx`](../src/features/music/NowPlayingPage.tsx) | fullscreen | NowPlaying |
| `/slideshow/:parentId [?index&id&start&recursive&sort&order&filter]` | [`features/photos/SlideshowPage.tsx`](../src/features/photos/SlideshowPage.tsx) | fullscreen | Slideshow |
| `/license` | [`features/settings/LicensePage.tsx`](../src/features/settings/LicensePage.tsx) | fullscreen | License |
| `/debug` | [`features/settings/DebugPage.tsx`](../src/features/settings/DebugPage.tsx) | fullscreen | Debug (no session needed: reachable from login failures) |
| `/dev/login [?next&server=test]` | `app/dev/DevLoginPage (DEV only)` | - | - |
| `/dev/gallery` | `ui/gallery/GalleryPage (DEV only)` | - | - |

## The project

```text
.
├── .github/  GitHub's own files: the checks that run on every push, the issue and pull-request forms
├── dev/  Things for the development machine only
├── docs/  The project's documents: what was done, decided and changed from the TV app, and this map
│   ├── screenshots/  The pictures the README shows
│   └── spec/  How the TV app behaves, written down from its source: what the web port follows
├── e2e/  The browser tests: they drive the real app in real browsers against the test server
│   ├── fixtures/  What every browser test starts from: sign-in, the app helper, the server helper, the settings
│   ├── flows/  Longer journeys through the app, played as tests
│   └── specs/  The browser tests themselves, one file per area of the app
├── public/  Files served as they are: the icon, the default settings file, the check for browsers that are too old
├── server/  The small production server: serves the built app, its settings, and passes requests on to Seerr
├── src/  The app itself: everything that runs in the browser
│   ├── api/  Talking to the servers: the Jellyfin sign-in and session, image addresses, shared data-loading helpers and the Seerr (Discover) connection
│   ├── app/  The frame of the app: start-up, routes, the shell around every page, error and loading screens, toasts, and the arrow-key navigation
│   ├── features/  One folder per area of the app (Home, Settings, the player ...): each screen and the parts only it uses
│   ├── i18n/  Languages: loading the chosen language, right-to-left handling and the text of every label in the app
│   ├── lib/  Small plain helpers with no screen of their own: time and number formatting, ids, browser storage and server-version checks
│   ├── stores/  What the app remembers: the saved preferences, the signed-in servers and users, remembered audio/subtitle choices and the music queue
│   ├── theme/  The look of the whole app: theme colours, text sizes, the interface scale and the global base styles
│   └── ui/  The shared parts every screen is built from: buttons, cards, rows, dialogs, menus, inputs, icons, spinners and helpers
├── tools/  Scripts for building and checking the project (generators, the screenshot crawler, the test server setup)
│   ├── code-map/  The hand-kept lists behind docs/CODE-MAP.md: what you see and where it is, one line per folder
│   ├── refshots/  Takes the reference pictures of the Android TV app in an emulator
│   ├── shots/  The screenshot crawler: photographs every screen of the web app and compares with the TV pictures
│   └── testserver/  Sets up the throwaway test server and generates its small test films and series
├── types/  Type descriptions for libraries that ship none
└── vendor/  Third-party code kept in the repository
```

## The source folder

```text
src/  The app itself: everything that runs in the browser
├── api/  Talking to the servers: the Jellyfin sign-in and session, image addresses, shared data-loading helpers and the Seerr (Discover) connection
│   ├── hooks/  Small shared data-loading hooks, for example the list of the user's libraries
│   ├── playback/  Builders for the media addresses the player uses: video streams, trickplay thumbnails, subtitles and attachments
│   └── seerr/  Everything for Seerr, the request service behind Discover: connection, sign-in, permissions, requests, search results and filters
├── app/  The frame of the app: start-up, routes, the shell around every page, error and loading screens, toasts, and the arrow-key navigation
│   ├── dev/  A developer-only sign-in page that is only available while running locally, not in the real site
│   └── shell/  The sidebar (nav drawer), the clock, the Back button, the backdrop picture, the copy of the page behind Settings, and focus/Back handling
├── features/  One folder per area of the app (Home, Settings, the player ...): each screen and the parts only it uses
│   ├── browse/  Library pages: movie/TV libraries with tabs, plain folders, favourites, genre/studio lists and the 'View more' grid
│   │   ├── components/  Parts of library pages: the grid, its header buttons (sort, filter, view options), tabs, list rows and the Recommended tab
│   │   ├── data/  What library pages ask the server: grid requests, paging, filter values, saved sort/filter/view state, Recommended rows
│   │   └── model/  Rules for library pages without any screen: sort lists, filters, view options, columns, letter jump, favourite types
│   ├── common/  Pieces many pages share: item right-click menu, card data, item text, image choice, hover delay, caches and library lists
│   ├── detail/  The detail pages opened from a card: movie, episode, series, box set, playlist and person, with the pieces they share
│   │   ├── collection/  The box-set (collection) page: its header, buttons, rows or grid of items, and its saved view options and sort
│   │   ├── common/  Pieces shared by the detail pages: header text, Play buttons, rows, track choosers, media info, playlists dialog
│   │   ├── episode/  The single-episode page, reached only for an episode without a series (normal episodes open in the series page)
│   │   ├── movie/  The movie page (also used for videos, music videos, recordings and trailers)
│   │   ├── person/  The page of an actor or crew member: photo, birth details, biography and their movies, shows and episodes
│   │   ├── playlist/  The playlist page: a library-style list of the playlist's items with Move up, Move down and More on each row
│   │   └── series/  The series pages: the series start page, and the season tabs with the episode strip and the focused episode's details
│   ├── discover/  Seerr: the Discover page and its tabs, movie/series/person pages, request dialogs, and the Seerr sign-in and settings entry
│   ├── home/  The Home page: its header, its rows of cards, the View more grid, and how Home remembers focus and scroll
│   │   ├── data/  Loading Home: which server requests each Home row makes, and how the rows are fetched and kept fresh
│   │   ├── model/  The data shape of Home rows: row types, display presets, and where the saved row list comes from (device, server, plugin)
│   │   └── settings/  The Customize home page screens: row list, add row, row options, presets, source, global settings, preview and its dialogs
│   ├── livetv/  Live TV: the Live TV page with its Guide, DVR Schedule and recording-folder tabs, the channel and program cells, and the recording dialogs
│   ├── music/  Music: album, artist, song and genre pages, the music library tabs, the Now Playing screen, the bottom mini player and the audio engine
│   │   ├── components/  Small shared music pieces: the album/artist header, the Play/Shuffle button strip, song rows, the playing marker and card rows
│   │   ├── data/  Where the music pages get their data from the server: item, lyrics and backdrop queries and the song lists a queue is filled from
│   │   ├── library/  The music library page's own pieces: its five tabs, the Recommended tab's rows and the artist list requests
│   │   ├── menu/  The right-click / three-dot menus of songs, albums, artists and queue rows on the music pages
│   │   ├── nowplaying/  The parts of the Now Playing screen: seek bar, queue list, lyrics, bar visualizer, view options and the changing backdrop
│   │   ├── queue/  The pure rules of the play queue: ordering, shuffle, repeat, moving and removing entries
│   │   └── service/  The music engine: the audio element, play/pause/next, stream address, progress reports to the server and the visualizer tap
│   ├── photos/  Photos: photo albums and libraries as a grid, the full-screen photo viewer and slideshow, the image filter, and the idle screensaver
│   ├── playback/  The player page: the video screen with its overlay, keys, pointer and touch handling, and the error screen
│   │   ├── engine/  The player's brain with no screen of its own: loads the stream, picks tracks, reports progress, draws subtitles on the video
│   │   └── ui/  Everything drawn over the video: control strip, buttons, seek bar, menus and sheets, skip, next up, debug panel, and the keys
│   ├── search/  The Search page: search bar, voice search, result rows or one combined grid, the Discover results and the search options
│   ├── settings/  Everything in Settings: the panel and its rows, the dialogs they open, the subtitle style editor, and the Debug and License pages
│   │   └── assets/  The sample picture (eclipse.jpeg) shown behind the example subtitles in the subtitle style editor
│   └── setup/  Everything before Home: the server picker, the user picker, the sign-in dialog, Quick Connect and the PIN screens
├── i18n/  Languages: loading the chosen language, right-to-left handling and the text of every label in the app
│   ├── extra/  The English texts that the Android app does not have and that the web version added (keys starting with web_)
│   └── locales/  One file of translated texts per language, plus the list of available languages; generated from the Android app
├── lib/  Small plain helpers with no screen of their own: time and number formatting, ids, browser storage and server-version checks
├── stores/  What the app remembers: the saved preferences, the signed-in servers and users, remembered audio/subtitle choices and the music queue
├── theme/  The look of the whole app: theme colours, text sizes, the interface scale and the global base styles
│   └── fonts/  The icon font (Font Awesome solid) used for the small icons in the sidebar and elsewhere
└── ui/  The shared parts every screen is built from: buttons, cards, rows, dialogs, menus, inputs, icons, spinners and helpers
    ├── assets/  The app logo pictures (the cube icon and the banner with the name) used by the logo component
    ├── buttons/  The pill buttons: normal, text, round icon, the Play-style button that opens to show its label, and the detail-page button row
    ├── cards/  Every card (poster, wide, grid, person, genre, chapter, server and user circles) plus their badges, pills and progress bar
    ├── feedback/  Spinners, the loading page, the error message block and the small toast pop-up messages
    ├── gallery/  A developer-only page (/dev/gallery) that shows every shared part side by side, with made-up pictures
    ├── icons/  The icon sets: Material icons, Font Awesome glyphs, the app's own drawn icons and the app logo
    ├── inputs/  Text boxes, the search box, the slider and the on/off switches
    ├── lib/  Behind-the-scenes helpers: focus and keyboard rules, mouse/touch scrolling, menu positions, text scrolling, colours from ids
    ├── overlays/  Pop-ups: the dialog shell, option lists, right-click menus, drop-down menus, confirm dialogs and the list rows inside them
    ├── rows/  Horizontal card rows with arrows, the scrolling card grid, the A-Z letter strip and the row loading placeholder
    └── text/  Text pieces: scrolling titles, overview text, rating stars, quick-details line, stream chips, the tab strip and logo-or-title
```

## Every file of the source folder

Each file with the first sentence of its own comment. A file is listed with its stylesheet (the look) and its test when it has them.

### src/

The app itself: everything that runs in the browser

- [`main.tsx`](../src/main.tsx)
- [`vite-env.d.ts`](../src/vite-env.d.ts)

### src/api/

Talking to the servers: the Jellyfin sign-in and session, image addresses, shared data-loading helpers and the Seerr (Discover) connection

- [`config.ts`](../src/api/config.ts): Deployment config served at /config.json (public/config.json, default `{}`). - serverUrl: when set, the app is locked to this one Jellyfin server and skips the server list. - serverName: display name fallback until…
- [`images.ts`](../src/api/images.ts) ([`test`](../src/api/images.test.ts)): Port of W/services/ImageUrlService.kt (spec 07 §7). URLs are built by hand (image routes are anonymous, no token is added), so they work in <img src> and stay cache-friendly thanks to `tag`.
- [`queryClient.ts`](../src/api/queryClient.ts): Exports queryClient.
- [`queryKeys.ts`](../src/api/queryKeys.ts): Query key scoped to the current server and user: `[serverId, userId, ...parts]`.
- [`session.ts`](../src/api/session.ts): Jellyfin client wiring and the server/user session lifecycle.

### src/api/hooks/

Small shared data-loading hooks, for example the list of the user's libraries

- [`useUserViews.ts`](../src/api/hooks/useUserViews.ts): The signed-in user's libraries (GET /UserViews). Shared by the nav drawer, home rows and settings, so there is exactly one query for it.

### src/api/playback/

Builders for the media addresses the player uses: video streams, trickplay thumbnails, subtitles and attachments

- [`urls.ts`](../src/api/playback/urls.ts): Playback URL builders (spec 05 §1.3, §4.2, §8). Media elements (<video>, <img>) cannot send an Authorization header, so these URLs carry the token as the `ApiKey` query parameter (spec 05 §B4 "Direct-play URL").

### src/api/seerr/

Everything for Seerr, the request service behind Discover: connection, sign-in, permissions, requests, search results and filters

- [`client.ts`](../src/api/seerr/client.ts) ([`test`](../src/api/seerr/client.test.ts)): Minimal Seerr HTTP client (port of W/api/seerr/SeerrApiClient.kt for a browser).
- [`endpoints.ts`](../src/api/seerr/endpoints.ts): The Seerr endpoints upstream calls (spec 04 §D.11), one typed function each.
- [`filter.ts`](../src/api/seerr/filter.ts): Discover grid sort/filter model (W/data/filter/DiscoverFilter.kt, W/util/DiscoverRequestPager.kt).
- [`index.ts`](../src/api/seerr/index.ts): Seerr (Jellyseerr/Overseerr) integration: proxy-relative client, per-user link, and the query hooks behind Discover.
- [`items.ts`](../src/api/seerr/items.ts): `DiscoverItem` and `SeerrService.createDiscoverItem` / `createImageUrl` (W/data/model/DiscoverItem.kt, W/services/SeerrService.kt).
- [`permissions.ts`](../src/api/seerr/permissions.ts): Seerr permission bits (port of W/data/model/SeerrPermission.kt, from Seerr server/lib/permissions.ts).
- [`queries.ts`](../src/api/seerr/queries.ts): TanStack Query hooks for the Seerr screens (the data side of SeerrDiscoverViewModel, DiscoverRequestViewModel, SeerrRequestsViewModel, DiscoverMovieViewModel, DiscoverSeriesViewModel, DiscoverPersonViewModel and…
- [`session.ts`](../src/api/seerr/session.ts): Seerr connection state per Jellyfin user (port of W/services/SeerrServerRepository.kt and W/services/UserSwitchListener.kt, adapted to a browser).
- [`status.ts`](../src/api/seerr/status.ts): Availability / request-status rules of the Seerr screens, kept pure so they can be unit tested.
- [`types.ts`](../src/api/seerr/types.ts): Hand-written subset of the Seerr OpenAPI document (reference/wholphin/app/src/main/seerr/seerr-api.yml) covering exactly the schemas the upstream client reads.
- [`seerr.test.ts`](../src/api/seerr/seerr.test.ts)

### src/app/

The frame of the app: start-up, routes, the shell around every page, error and loading screens, toasts, and the arrow-key navigation

- [`App.tsx`](../src/app/App.tsx): Exports App.
- [`applyPreferences.ts`](../src/app/applyPreferences.ts): Keeps `<html data-theme>`, the interface scale and the UI language in sync with preferences.
- [`AppShell.tsx`](../src/app/AppShell.tsx): App shell for drawer pages (W/ui/nav/ApplicationContent.kt + NavDrawer.kt): backdrop behind everything, the nav drawer (64dp rail that expands on hover / keyboard focus / tap; an overlay sheet on phones), the page…
- [`backdrop.ts`](../src/app/backdrop.ts): Backdrop requests (upstream W/services/BackdropService.kt). Pages call submitBackdrop(item) when an item gains focus/hover or a detail page opens, and clearBackdrop() when nothing should show.
- [`ErrorBoundary.tsx`](../src/app/ErrorBoundary.tsx): Last-resort boundary around the whole app (React error boundaries must be classes).
- [`ErrorScreen.tsx`](../src/app/ErrorScreen.tsx) ([`styles`](../src/app/ErrorScreen.module.css)): Error message page (upstream `ErrorMessage`): title, message and a reload / home action.
- [`layouts.tsx`](../src/app/layouts.tsx): Root of every route: waits for the startup restore, then renders; hosts toasts, window scroll restoration, focus restoration on Back and the history mirror the drawer uses.
- [`LoadingScreen.tsx`](../src/app/LoadingScreen.tsx) ([`styles`](../src/app/LoadingScreen.module.css)): Full-screen centred spinner (upstream LoadingPage / setup `Loading`).
- [`nav.ts`](../src/app/nav.ts): Typed path builders for every route in routes.tsx. Never hand-build app URLs elsewhere.
- [`NotFoundPage.tsx`](../src/app/NotFoundPage.tsx): Exports NotFoundPage.
- [`providers.tsx`](../src/app/providers.tsx): Exports Providers.
- [`RouteError.tsx`](../src/app/RouteError.tsx): Route-level errorElement: loader/lazy-import failures and render errors inside a route.
- [`routes.tsx`](../src/app/routes.tsx): Route table. Every upstream Destination (W/ui/nav/Destination.kt, spec 02 §2.1) mapped to a URL.
- [`spatialNav.ts`](../src/app/spatialNav.ts) ([`test`](../src/app/spatialNav.test.ts)): Global arrow-key spatial navigation (the D-pad of the TV app) for elements marked `data-focusable`.
- [`startup.ts`](../src/app/startup.ts): App start (MainActivityViewModel.appStart): scale, preferences side effects, i18n, keyboard navigation, then the session restore runs in the background while RootLayout shows a spinner.
- [`toast.ts`](../src/app/toast.ts): Shows a transient message at the bottom of the screen (upstream `showToast`).
- [`ToastContainer.tsx`](../src/app/ToastContainer.tsx) ([`styles`](../src/app/ToastContainer.module.css)): Toasts, drawn above everything like an Android Toast. In <body>, next to the dialogs: the app root is its own stacking context (global.css), so from inside it a toast would sit under an open dialog's scrim.
- [`useScrollRestore.ts`](../src/app/useScrollRestore.ts): Remembers and restores the scroll position of a nested scroll container for the current history entry, so Back returns to where the user was (window scrolling is handled by <ScrollRestoration/>). const ref =…
- [`useSetupTarget.ts`](../src/app/useSetupTarget.ts): Where a signed-out visitor must go: user list when a server is chosen (or preset), else the server list.
- [`globals.d.ts`](../src/app/globals.d.ts)
- [`spatialNav.dom.test.ts`](../src/app/spatialNav.dom.test.ts)

### src/app/dev/

A developer-only sign-in page that is only available while running locally, not in the real site

- [`DevLoginPage.tsx`](../src/app/dev/DevLoginPage.tsx): DEV ONLY (registered in routes.tsx under import.meta.env.DEV): signs in through the Vite middleware GET /__dev/session (tools/vite-dev-session.ts), which reads the test credentials server-side.…

### src/app/shell/

The sidebar (nav drawer), the clock, the Back button, the backdrop picture, the copy of the page behind Settings, and focus/Back handling

- [`BackButton.tsx`](../src/app/shell/BackButton.tsx) ([`styles`](../src/app/shell/BackButton.module.css)): Web-only Back control (the TV remote's Back button). Goes back in history, or to Home when the page was opened directly.
- [`Backdrop.tsx`](../src/app/shell/Backdrop.tsx) ([`styles`](../src/app/shell/Backdrop.module.css)): W/ui/nav/Backdrop.kt: full-window layer behind the drawer pages.

### src/ui/lib/

Behind-the-scenes helpers: focus and keyboard rules, mouse/touch scrolling, menu positions, text scrolling, colours from ids

- [`bringIntoView.ts`](../src/ui/lib/bringIntoView.ts) ([`test`](../src/ui/lib/bringIntoView.test.ts)): Scrolling a newly focused element into place the way the TV app does.
- [`contextMenu.ts`](../src/ui/lib/contextMenu.ts): Where to open a context menu for a `contextmenu` event: the pointer position for a mouse/pen right-click, or `null` (open as the centered TV-style dialog) for the keyboard Menu key / Shift+F10 and for touch long-press.
- [`dragScroll.ts`](../src/ui/lib/dragScroll.ts) ([`test`](../src/ui/lib/dragScroll.test.ts)): Mouse drag-scroll for a horizontally scrolling row: press, pull sideways, release.
- [`fieldArrowExit.ts`](../src/ui/lib/fieldArrowExit.ts) ([`test`](../src/ui/lib/fieldArrowExit.test.ts)): Which way an arrow key should move focus out of a one-line text field, or null when the key belongs to the caret.
- [`focus.ts`](../src/ui/lib/focus.ts): Tab-reachable, visible descendants of `root` in DOM order.
- [`gridMath.ts`](../src/ui/lib/gridMath.ts): Column math for `CardGrid`. Upstream (`ui/detail/CardGrid.kt:330-345`) uses a fixed column count from the view options and computes card width = ceil((width - spacing * (columns - 1)) / columns).
